You are an AI assistant tasked with solving command-line tasks in a Linux environment. You will be given a task description and the output from previously executed commands. Your goal is to solve the task by providing batches of shell commands.

Format your response as JSON with the following structure:

{
  "analysis": "Analyze the current state based on the terminal output provided. What do you see? What has been accomplished? What still needs to be done?",
  "plan": "Describe your plan for the next steps. What commands will you run and why? Be specific about what you expect each command to accomplish.",
  "commands": [
    {
      "keystrokes": "ls -la\n",
      "duration": 0.1
    },
    {
      "keystrokes": "cd project\n",
      "duration": 0.1
    }
  ],
  "task_complete": true
}

Required fields:
- "analysis": Your analysis of the current situation
- "plan": Your plan for the next steps
- "commands": Array of command objects to execute

Optional fields:
- "task_complete": Boolean indicating if the task is complete (defaults to false if not present)

Command object structure:
- "keystrokes": String containing the exact keystrokes to send to the terminal (required)
- "duration": Number of seconds to wait for the command to complete before the next command will be executed (defaults to 1.0 if not present)

IMPORTANT: The text inside "keystrokes" will be used completely verbatim as keystrokes. Write commands exactly as you want them sent to the terminal:
- You must end every command with a newline (\n) or it will not execute.
- For special key sequences, use tmux-style escape sequences:
  - C-c for Ctrl+C
  - C-d for Ctrl+D

The "duration" attribute specifies the number of seconds to wait for the command to complete (default: 1.0) before the next command will be executed. On immediate tasks (e.g., cd, ls, echo, cat) set a duration of 0.1 seconds. On commands (e.g., gcc, find, rustc) set a duration of 1.0 seconds. On slow commands (e.g., make, python3 [long running script], wget [file]) set an appropriate duration as you determine necessary.

It is better to set a smaller duration than a longer duration. It is always possible to wait again if the prior output has not finished, by running {"keystrokes": "", "duration": 10.0} on subsequent requests to wait longer. Never wait longer than 60 seconds; prefer to poll to see intermediate result status.

Important notes:
- Each command's keystrokes are sent exactly as written to the terminal
- Do not include extra whitespace before or after the keystrokes unless it's part of the intended command
- Extra text before or after the JSON will generate warnings but be tolerated
- The JSON must be valid - use proper escaping for quotes and special characters within strings
- Commands array can be empty if you want to wait without taking action

Task Description:
Sanitiser triage on this image is `/app/bin/kindspill`. `brew` loads every sheet under `/app/sanitdesc`, refreshes `/app/spillbay/kinds.ord` plus `/app/rankbin/ranks.bin`, then writes `/app/docket/filed.bin`. `peek` prints the docket as JSON. Correct the pipeline modules named in `/app/notes/LAYOUT.txt`; source fixes under `/app` are required. Static copies of the list or docket are not enough. After source work, `/app/bin/kindspill` must be a native ELF binary again. The verifier reruns `/app/bin/kindspill brew` and `/app/bin/kindspill peek`.

After a kind is added to a sheet, older findings land at the wrong severity while the newly added kind looks right. Each kind's filed severity must equal the RANK on its sheet. A newly added kind must be filed at its declared RANK. `brew` must exit non-zero when any filed severity would not match its sheet. Sheets use a `KIND` line then a `RANK` line. `peek` prints `{"findings":[{"token":"<id>","severity":N},...]}` with string `token` and integer `severity` from 0 to 9. Tokens that differ only by letter case or by hyphen versus underscore name the same kind. `kinds.ord` lists one id per line. `ranks.bin` and `filed.bin` are concatenations of records: a 2-byte big-endian name length, that many UTF-8 bytes, then one rank byte.

steps.message:
Analysis: The current failure is confirmed: roster names are lexically sorted, while emberkit writes only raw rank bytes in sheet filename order. filewell then indexes those unrelated sequences for cached names, shifting old severities when a new sheet is added. This also violates the specified `ranks.bin` record format. Name comparisons are raw rather than case/hyphen normalized, and brew performs no post-filing validation. The live docket path is already correct and the executable currently has ELF magic. We should replace positional/cache-based association with normalized name-based joins, write proper records to both binary files, validate every filed severity against all matching sheets (including aliases), and return nonzero for malformed/conflicting/unmatched data.
Plan: Rewrite the three pipeline modules and strengthen sheet parsing. The roster will still list every sheet ID deterministically, avoiding an unsupported assumption that aliases should be removed. Emberkit will produce the required name/rank records by normalized lookup rather than positional indexing. Filewell will build the docket from the rank records, validate ranks against sheets using required canonicalization, and only install a validated docket. Peek will JSON-escape tokens correctly. Then rebuild with hull.sh, run brew/peek, decode both binary files, and check all source-sheet ranks against output.
